title: Per-tenant shadow evals with local reference corpora
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a per-tenant "shadow eval" pipeline that runs model/config changes against customer-scoped reference corpora that never leave the customer boundary (VPC or on-prem). The goal is to detect quality regressions specific to a customer's prompt/response distribution and to surface automated regression gates in the Console for Dedicated and Private customers. This must preserve data sovereignty: reference corpora are encrypted and can be run only in the customer's environment or a customer-managed enclave.

Scope: Implement the evaluation orchestration, tenant artifact registration, result ingestion into Console dashboards and rollout gating. Provide a lightweight on-prem runner and a VPC-first hosted runner pattern for Dedicated customers. Do not include building global model-level eval benchmarks (out of scope).

Why: Customers with regulatory constraints or unique prompt distributions need per-tenant signal to avoid silent quality regressions when we change kernels, quantization profiles, batching defaults, or model variants. A single global eval can miss tenant-specific regressions.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement automated remediation (model rollback orchestration) nor the full audit-log export work for Private on-prem upgrades (those are separate tasks).
acceptance_criteria: A1: For a given tenant, team can register an encrypted reference corpus artifact (s3-compatible URL or on-prem path) and associate it with an eval suite.
A2: On every model/config change on the candidate rollout path, the system can trigger a shadow eval that executes only inside the tenant boundary (hosted VPC or on-prem runner).

A3: Eval results are returned as aggregated metrics (precision/recall, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, hallucination-rate, response-time distribution) and appear in the tenant Console under 'Regression Watchdogs' within 30 minutes of completion.

A4: Admins can opt to mark an eval suite as 'block rollout on regression' or 'inform-only'; when blocked, the rollout API returns a non-zero status and the Console highlights the failure with links to evidence.
A5: No customer reference corpus or raw test outputs leave the tenant boundary unencrypted; metadata and aggregated metrics must be designed to avoid leaking PII.
updates: 2026-02-10 - Created ticket and scoped initial requirements after demo with two enterprise pilot customers (FinServCo, HealthApp). These customers requested: per-tenant sensitivity for hallucination regressions and the ability to block canary rollouts.

2026-02-18 - PM/Eng sync: agreed on two-runner model: 'local-runner' for on-prem and 'vpc-runner' for Dedicated VPCs. ENG requested narrower initial metric set to reduce runtime: (hallucination-rate, task-accuracy, median-latency).

2026-02-26 - Design feedback: UX should surface (1) last-run summary, (2) diff vs baseline, (3) links to example failing prompts. Design to produce red/amber/green color-coding. Designer assigned: Maya Ortiz.

2026-03-02 - Security review kickoff: security team requested KMS integration for tenant artifact keys and an HSM-backed key wrap. Noted requirement for 'no exfil' proof during audit. Security review flagged data retention policy for eval logs.

2026-03-09 - Engineering spike (ENG-2012) completed: prototype runner executes test harness in a confined container with mounted encrypted corpus; takes ~12m for 10k examples on a T4 equivalent. Performance optimizations needed for scale. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/688

2026-03-12 - PM review: prioritized initial pilot with FinServCo and HealthApp. Decided to ship 'inform-only' mode first, then flip to 'block rollout' after two successful pilots and the security sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer corpora sizes may make per-change evals expensive and slow. Mitigation: support sampled suites, incremental eval (only changed config dimensions), and nightly full-sweeps for non-blocking coverage.

Risk: Leakage of sensitive content via logs or example snippets. Mitigation: mask PII in failing examples by default and require explicit tenant admin opt-in to view raw snippets; encrypt at rest and in transit; KMS/HSM integration required.

Risk: Increased CI/infra cost for frequent rollouts. Mitigation: rate-limit per-tenant eval frequency and provide cost-estimates in Console; enable customers to choose cadence (on-change, nightly, weekly).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): implement runner + minimal Console UI; 'inform-only' mode for two pilot customers. (Apr 2026)
Phase 1 (beta): expose tenant eval suites in Console, support 'block rollout' toggle behind enterprise flag; expand to 10 dedicated customers. (May 2026)
Phase 2 (GA): harden security review items, autoscale runner fleet, add audit-log export and synthetic augmentation tooling. (Jun 2026)
Rollback policy: initial block only prevents promotion on our orchestrator; we will not auto-rollback customer-managed deployments without explicit runbook.
outstanding_decisions: 1) Finalize allowed metrics set for initial pilot (proposal: hallucination-rate, task-accuracy, median-latency). Action: ENG to confirm implementation cost by 2026-03-20.
2) Decide storage model for tenant artifacts: encrypted S3 with customer KMS vs local on-prem path. Action: Security + Solutions to draft prescriptive guidance.
3) UX: whether to expose failing example text by default or hide behind admin permission. Action: Design to prototype both flows and test with pilot customers.
notes_for_engineering: Build secure runner API that accepts (1) encrypted artifact locator and (2) eval-suite manifest; runner must not emit raw artifact content over the network.
Provide a lightweight local runner binary for on-prem customers with attestation and heartbeat reporting back to Control Plane (metadata-only).
Expose an internal 'eval-run' webhook that the deployment pipeline can call to gate rollouts; return structured signal (ok/warn/fail) with metric deltas.
Add feature-flag to toggle 'block rollout on regression' per-tenant.
